correctness.rationale: For A with m>=2 pairwise-annihilating branches x_i and lengths d_i>=3, differentiating x_i x_j=0 forces D(x_i) to contain own branch powers x_i...x_i^(d_i-1) and only other-branch top monomials x_j^(d_j-1). The bracket formula [E_ia,E_ib]=(b-a)E_i,a+b-1, [C,C]=0 and Euler-branch action on C gives the first commutator ideal. In char2 all and only even-index E lie in L^(1) and commute with one another and C, so L^(2)=0. In all other characteristics, [F_{i,r},F_{i,r}]=F_{i,2r} follows from two candidate commutator coefficients differing by 2, implying dimensions sum max(d_i-2^j,0), j>=2, and exact derived length ceil(log2(max d_i)). The branch dimension and both abelianization dimensions follow. Independent bracket-template calculations for all d=3..10 over p=2,3,5,7 agree, with the source verification solving the differentiated relations from scratch for 12 finite cases. The proof, not these finite tests, covers arbitrary fields.
